questions.question: Describe how update() and setdefault() methods work and when to use each, with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how update() and setdefault() methods work and when to use each,
  • with examples. / [CO3]
  • Ans: update() method: Updates a dictionary with key:value pairs from another dictionary. If a
  • key exists, its value is overwritten. If it doesn’t exist, the new key:value pair is added.
  • - Used to merge dictionaries or add/update multiple key:value pairs at once.
  • Example:
  • d = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}
  • d.update({'b': 5, 'c': 3})
  • print(d) # Output: {'a': 1, 'b': 5, 'c': 3}
  • Here `'b'` was updated and `'c'` was added.
  • setdefault()method: Returns the value of a key if it exists. If the key doesn’t exist, it inserts the
  • key with a specified default value and returns that value.
  • When you want to get a key’s value, but also ensure the key exists in the dictionary with a
  • default if it was missing. Useful for initializing values.
  • Example:
  • d = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}
  • val1 = d.setdefault('b', 100) # 'b' exists, so returns 2
  • val2 = d.setdefault('c', 100) # 'c' missing, adds 'c':100 and returns 100
  • print(d) # Output: {'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 100}
  • print(val1, val2) # Output: 2 100

questions.question: Explain the flow of execution in a Python program that includes function definitions and function calls. Describe how control moves between the calling function and the function definition with an example. [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the flow of execution in a Python program that includes function definitions and
  • function calls. Describe how control moves between the calling function and the function
  • definition with an example. / [CO3]
  • Ans: Python is an interpreted language. The interpreter reads code from top to bottom and
  • executes it line by line. However, when functions are present, execution does not always stay
  • linear. Control "jumps" between different parts of the program.
  • Function definition:When Python sees `def function_name():`, it creates a function object in
  • memory and binds the name to it. The code inside the function is *not executed* at this point.
  • Function call: When Python sees `function_name()`, it suspends the current flow, jumps to the
  • first line of the function body, executes it, then returns back to the point after the call.
  • Explanation on function definition and call and flow of control – (8 marks)
  • Program with function definition and call and explanation of control flow in that program - (7 marks)
